strings.name: Eric Maskin
strings.role: Economist · Mechanism design and social choice
strings.summary: Maskin uses mathematics to study incentives, institutional rules and social choice, including how public goals can be implemented when individuals hold private information. He taught at MIT, Harvard and the Institute for Advanced Study before returning to Harvard in 2012. He shared the 2007 economics Nobel with Hurwicz and Myerson, and continues researching voting, contracts and inequality.

strings.highlights.h1.title: Implementing social goals
strings.highlights.h1.text: Developed theory analyzing how rules and individual incentives can implement social goals.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Social choice and voting
strings.highlights.h2.text: Applies economic theory to voting rules and electoral-reform proposals.
